# Controlled evaluation authority: Working timing

This explicit CF-07 evaluation amendment supersedes only the Working frame duration
of 100 ms in the preserved historical BRIEF.md and src/queue-view.ts. The current
authorized duration is 150 ms per frame, four frames, looping, a 600 ms cycle.
src/working-timing.ts is the dedicated executable timing source. The stable
src/queue-view-integration.ts wrapper applies it to display.frameMs in the actual
renderer while reusing both original statusCell and compactStatus consumers.

All other brief requirements and the retained source-defined visual roles remain.
Reuse the exact existing assets/working.png bytes; this is a timing integration
change, with no new art or provider execution authorized. All five original art
files and original shared sources must remain unchanged. Inspect real rendered
stills in both consumers at 1x and 3x nearest on the existing dark panel. Observe
actual live loop playback at the consumer's enlarged 3x scale in both consumers.
Native 1x live playback remains unperformed; controlled 1x frame-boundary samples
are a separate observation. The original brief requires 1x/3x inspection, not live
playback at every inspection scale.
Fresh current review and acceptance must not be inferred from historical evidence.

# Asset brief

Create coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone.

Assets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.

Update: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.

Current update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.

# Review the representative style and render the existing consumers
Continue the retained Ready delivery and corrected prospective contract. Inspect
the actual supplied art and the prior assessment, verify factual descriptions,
and decide whether this sample should guide the remaining status family under the
brief. You are authorized to make the scoped caller style decision for this
representative consumer using PIXL's recommendations and your independent review.
Preserve the historical request, contracts, verdicts, candidate and provider records;
any new review or acceptance must identify its own scope and evidence.

The consumer now has a runnable browser entry point in renderer/. It imports the
actual src/queue.ts and src/queue-view.ts and uses the mapped image files. Run
node renderer/capture.mjs --out work/NEW_CAPTURE_DIRECTORY
to retain browser observations, native/enlarged panel views and destination.png.
Use the selected Python with renderer/check.py --project . --capture DIRECTORY
to independently check retained identities, screenshot pixels and available PNG
compositing/scaling. That checker does not supply the visual/style decision.
Create the parent work directory if needed. The command detects an installed local
Chrome/Edge and uses a separate temporary profile. A new capture requires a new
output directory. Inspect the resulting images through the host's image tools;
the report alone supplies no visual verdict. Do not edit the renderer to obtain
a passing capture. Use its measured facts, actual source modules and observed
screen to assess sampling, alpha compositing, placement and backend-to-view mapping
in both consumers. This stage supplies a representative browser renderer; it does
not retroactively change earlier no-renderer observations.

Review the family as it actually exists. Preserve the existing Start vector and
all source requirements, distinguish absent members from rejected ones, and retain
an actionable continuation for remaining members. Do not manufacture replacement
images, a completed family, provider activity or reviews of nonexistent artwork.
Update the consumer's PLAR/workflow through the appropriate existing operations,
preserving history and meaningful requirements. Separate sample/style adoption,
available-member destination acceptance, collective family acceptance and actual
PixelLab-generated quality. The latter is not established by this controlled sample.
